bull.t: Large contracted backlog and 1 GW award
bull.b: A ~$543M contracted backlog and a 1 GW award give durable revenue visibility and production runway. This supports multi-quarter manufacturing utilization, reduces near-term sales volatility, and enables phased execution of projects that underpin medium-term revenue realization.

bull.t: New CEO with renewables and storage experience
bull.b: Appointment of Anthony Carroll, who has renewables and energy storage experience and performance-based compensation, signals a governance reset. Seasoned leadership can improve strategic execution, strengthen developer/EPC relationships, and better align incentives for multi-quarter operational improvements.

bull.t: Specialized utility-scale solar tracker business model
bull.b: FTC Solar's focused product and services mix—single-axis trackers plus engineering and software—aligns with structural utility-scale solar growth. Specialization creates aftermarket, installation and software revenue opportunities that can deliver recurring demand beyond single project sales.

bear.t: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained cash burn (TTM OpCF ~-$37.7M; FCF ~-$39.1M) forces reliance on external capital and limits internal funding for manufacturing, inventory and R&D. Continued negative cash generation elevates liquidity risk and constrains the company’s ability to scale operations while executing backlog.

bear.t: Negative stockholders' equity and weakened balance sheet
bear.b: Negative shareholders' equity (~-$6.1M) reflects a materially weakened balance sheet. This reduces borrowing flexibility, raises refinancing and covenant risk, and limits the firm's capacity to absorb cost overruns or delays when delivering large utility-scale projects without fresh capital.

bear.t: Deeply negative margins and operating losses
bear.b: Very low gross margin (~3.5%) and steep net/EBIT losses (~-42% and ~-54%) show the business has not reached a sustainable cost structure. Even with revenue improvements, such margin profiles require structural pricing or cost changes to achieve sustained profitability within the medium term.
